description: Guard against validator-class subagents issuing mutation Bash commands. validator-bash-guard.sh must emit permissionDecision: 'deny' for the 7 validator agents (code-reviewer, code-explorer, code-architect, comment-analyzer, pr-test-analyzer, silent-failure-hunter, security-reviewer) when they issue git push / rm / sed -i / curl POST etc. The BLOCK signal is in the JSON hookSpecificOutput (NOT the exit code — Claude Code's PreToolUse contract reads permissionDecision from the JSON, not the exit status). If this guard disappears or the JSON contract is broken, the audit F1 fix (commit `2d3c743`) regresses — validators regain the ability to mutate while supposedly inspecting (ref: bounded-agent-spawning memory).

evals.task: Run validator-bash-guard.sh with stdin simulating a validator agent (agent_type=code-reviewer) issuing 'git push'. The hook must emit hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision='deny' in JSON to stdout.
success_criteria: Output contains hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision equal to deny
Output contains the mutation pattern name (git push)
Output contains the agent name (code-reviewer) in the reason

evals.task: Run validator-bash-guard.sh with stdin having NO agent_type (main thread / non-validator). The hook must emit NO permissionDecision JSON (fail-open for non-validator calls is the documented contract, hook line 22: 'Fail-open for non-validator agents and main-thread').
success_criteria: Output does not contain permissionDecision (fail-open means no decision emitted)
Hook does not block the call
